title: Vendor Evidence Preservation and Subpoena Response Guide
summary: Operational playbook for preserving forensic evidence, responding to subpoenas or lawful process involving customer data and vendor-provided systems. Focused on Redwood Inference hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and vendor relationships.
body:
Purpose:
This guide defines the steps Redwood Inference takes when faced with a subpoena, search warrant, law enforcement request, or other legal process that implicates customer data, vendor-hosted infrastructure, or on-prem/private deployments. It balances legal obligations, customer confidentiality, data minimization, and chain-of-custody best practices.

Scope:
Applies to all requests directed at Redwood corporate systems, hosted API logs and artifacts, Dedicated pools, Private deployments where Redwood has responsibility for evidence, and interactions with third-party vendors and subprocessors that may hold relevant material. Does NOT replace customer-specific contractual obligations; where a contract or DPA specifies a different process, follow the contract and notify Legal.

Key definitions:
- Evidence: any logs, stored model inputs/outputs, runtime artifacts, telemetry, backups, snapshots, encryption metadata, KMS logs, and configuration state that might be relevant to legal process.
- Legal Hold: formal instruction to preserve specific categories of data pending legal process.
- Custodian: individual or team responsible for a data set or system (e.g., SRE on-call for serving runtime; Solutions engineer for Private installs).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Legal (Primary): receive process, assess validity, coordinate with counsel, prepare court filings if necessary, and approve disclosures.
- Security & Compliance (Evidence Lead): preserve volatile artifacts, create forensic snapshots, record chain-of-custody, and liaise with SRE/infra.
- SRE / Platform Ops: execute safe snapshots, export logs, and maintain operational stability.
- Customer Success / Account Lead: notify impacted customers when contract or law requires notice; coordinate information shared with them.
- Vendor Management: engage third-party suppliers; request preservation / evidence from vendor per contractual onboarding playbook.

Immediate actions (first 24 hours) after receiving a request:
1) Do not acknowledge production of any data externally. Direct all external requests to Legal.
2) Legal triages: is the request valid (jurisdiction, proper service)? If unclear, escalate to outside counsel immediately.
3) If valid and potentially urgent, Legal issues a preservation notice internally and sets Legal Hold.
4) Security & Compliance stands up an Evidence Task Force and assigns a Custodian for each relevant system.
5) SRE creates immutable snapshots of relevant environments (logs, KV cache dumps, model session exports) using documented tooling; where possible preserve compute state without powering down to avoid data loss.
6) Preserve related KMS logs, access records, and audit trails (rotation events, key access). Note whether keys are customer-managed (bring this to Legal and Customer Success).

Evidence preservation checklist (technical):
- API request logs (time-range specified) with request IDs and upstream client identifiers.
- Worker/gpu host console output and systemd/journal logs for time window.
- Model runtime artifacts: KV cache captures, prefix cache dumps, and any in-memory sequence buffers exported via tracing framework where feasible.
- Storage snapshots: object store manifests, snapshot IDs, and checksums.
- Backups: relevant backup identifiers and retention tombstones.
- KMS and HSM access logs (key use, wrapping/unwrapping events).
- Authentication and access logs (IAM events, tokens issued, refresh cycles).
- Network flow metadata where retained (not packet captures unless ordered).
- Dashboards and observability traces (sample traces linked to relevant requestIDs).

Chain-of-custody template (to be completed for each artifact):
- Artifact ID: 
- Description: 
- System / Host: 
- Time range captured: 
- Method of capture (snapshot, export tool, API): 
- Person executing capture: 
- Storage location (immutable): 
- Checksum / hash (sha256): 
- Date/time of capture: 
- Transfer log (who received artifact): 
- Legal review status: 

Preservation notes for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments:
- If a customer hosts Redwood runtime in their VPC/on-prem and Redwood has no access, instruct Legal to request the customer to preserve artifacts and provide escalation language. Use the contract annex for evidence-handback timelines.
- For Private deployments where Redwood retains a management channel, preserve only what is contractually permitted. Coordinate with Customer Success to limit exposure.

Vendor/subprocessor coordination:
- If the relevant artifact lives with a vendor, Vendor Management issues a preservation request under contract and documents the vendor’s acknowledgement.
- If vendor refuses or delays, Legal documents objections and may seek court process naming the vendor.
- Maintain a single ticket (Jira security/evidence) per legal process to capture all vendor communications and timestamps.

Disclosure process and minimality principle:
- Legal approves any disclosure. Aim to disclose the minimum responsive set of artifacts. Prefer exports that redact unrelated customer identifiers where feasible. Maintain an internal log of redaction decisions.
- If court orders full production, document attempt to limit scope and the reason for broader production.

Sample internal Legal Hold notice (short):
"Legal Hold: matter SEC-2024-1876. All engineering, SRE, and platform teams must preserve logs and runbook artifacts for environment rwinf-prod-1 between 2024-08-01 and 2024-08-15. Do not delete snapshots or rotate relevant keys until Legal releases the hold. Contact Legal (legal@redwood.ai) for questions."

Sample external cover letter for production (to be reviewed by counsel):
[Letterhead]
Re: Response to [Process Type] dated [date]
Attached please find the responsive artifacts we are producing for matter [identifier]. These artifacts were preserved as described in our chain-of-custody records. Where permissible we have redacted non-responsive identifiers. If you believe additional artifacts are needed, please provide a narrowly tailored request and proof of authority.

Retention and post-matter disposition:
- After matter closure, Legal authorizes secure deletion or long-term retention depending on follow-up obligations. Maintain chain-of-custody records for at least seven years unless stronger retention is required by law or contract.
- For artifacts moved to long-term evidence storage, encrypt at rest and record access controls.

Cross-border and data residency considerations:
- Identify nationality of requesting authority. If the request implicates EU/UK personal data, Legal assesses adequacy (MLATs, mutual assistance) and consults Data Protection Officer. Avoid extrajudicial disclosures without appropriate legal basis.
- For customer data under residency requirements, first inform Customer Success/Account Lead; some contracts require notice and a right to contest.

Operational tooling and ticketing:
- Create a ticket in Jira with prefix SEC-EVIDENCE and link to all artifacts. Use the Evidence Task Force Slack channel for real-time coordination and pin the chain-of-custody doc.
- Use S3 immutable buckets or equivalent for artifact storage with object locks enabled.

Escalation matrix and SLA expectations:
- Within 2 hours: Legal acknowledges receipt of process and assigns Legal case owner.
- Within 6 hours: Security & Compliance assembles Evidence Task Force and identifies custodians.
- Within 24–48 hours: First certified snapshot delivered to Legal for counsel review.
- If immediate production is demanded and jurisdiction forces same-day compliance, Legal coordinates with outside counsel and documents necessity and scope.

Training and auditability:
- Quarterly tabletop exercises with Security, SRE, Legal, and Solutions Engineering to validate playbook.
- Annual audit of preservation tooling, immutable storage, and chain-of-custody logs.

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers called to preserve data:
- Stop any automated deletion jobs for the named time window.
- Do not rotate or destroy keys tied to evidence. Note key identifiers.
- Run the evidence-export script available in infra/tools/evidence-export and capture stdout to artifact storage.
- Note the exact git commit and deployment tag for the environment.
- Add all steps to the Jira SEC-EVIDENCE ticket.

Notes and references:
- See confluence:SEC-EVIDENCE-PROC-2024 for tooling docs.
- Contract clause references: evidence-handback annex in standard Private Deployment DPA (search "evidence-handback").
- Related Jira: SEC-2024-1876 contains an open example case and retrospective notes.
